title: Gene Expression Analysis and RNA-Seq Protocol
author: Frank O Aylward
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.v4qe8vw

steps.title: Identify highly expressed genes for T1 sample
steps.instruction: Use BEDTools to intersect the sorted BAM file for the 15-minute time-point (T1) with the genome BED file to count reads mapping to specific features.

substeps.instruction: Run the intersection command: bedtools intersect -a D29.bed -c -bed -f 0.2 -b T1.sort.bam > intersect_T1.txt
Identify the top 5 most highly expressed genes by sorting the output: sort -k 11,11 -rn intersect_T1.txt | cut -f 10,11 | head -n 5

steps.title: Process RNA-Seq data for T2 sample
steps.instruction: Prepare the 60-minute time-point (T2) data by downloading, mapping, and sorting the reads.

substeps.instruction: Download the FASTQ file: fastq-dump -X 10000 SRR5585002
Map reads using bowtie2: bowtie2 -U SRR5585002.fastq -x D29 -S T2.sam
Filter unmapped reads and convert to BAM: samtools view -bS -F 4 T2.sam > T2.bam
Sort the BAM file: samtools sort T2.bam T2.sort
Index the BAM file: samtools index T2.sort.bam

steps.title: Identify highly expressed genes for T2 sample
steps.instruction: Perform the intersection and sorting analysis on the T2 sample to identify late-stage expressed genes.

substeps.instruction: Run the intersection command: bedtools intersect -a D29.bed -c -bed -f 0.2 -b T2.sort.bam > intersect_T2.txt
Identify the top 5 most highly expressed genes: sort -k 11,11 -rn intersect_T2.txt | cut -f 10,11 | head -n 5

steps.title: Compare T1 and T2 expression levels
steps.instruction: Combine the results from both time-points into a single file for side-by-side comparison.

substeps.instruction: Merge the intersection files: paste intersect_T1.txt intersect_T2.txt > combined_mapping.txt
Extract gene names and read counts for both samples: cut -f 10,11,22 combined_mapping.txt | head
Sort by T1 expression (column 2): cut -f 10,11,22 combined_mapping.txt | sort -rn -k 2,2 | head
Sort by T2 expression (column 3): cut -f 10,11,22 combined_mapping.txt | sort -rn -k 3,3 | head
